is a scripted fake that has no entry leftrefused, script_exhaustedscripting one entry per step the test runs
is a scripted step naming a tool outside read_toolsrefused, tool_not_read_classnaming only read tools, or proposing the call

An invalid request, or a step input for another node, is not a result: run_agent_step raises ContractValidationError (for example attempt: violates minimum 1) before anything runs. The request's limits are enforced by this boundary for every adapter (below). The interpreter reserves the step's tokens before calling it and settles them after (B08.4). Not covered here, so not claimed: a blocking adapter is not interrupted. The interpreter calls run_agent_step only for a plan that carries a governed-step context, and then records the proposal it returns (Governed agent steps: a protected action is a proposal).

OpenAI Responses governed step (B08.openai-responses, #730)#

OpenAIResponsesWorkflowExecutor.run_step runs one bounded governed step through client.responses.create; the adapter is caliber.workflows.step_openai_responses and the existing ungoverned run_agent path is unchanged. It adds no route, table or setting; step_clock is an optional test clock, defaulting to UTC now.

  • Tools. Read tools are offered with their normal Responses function schema and are executed only from step_input.read_tools. Every other bound tool is offered with a strict proposal envelope (connector, connector_version, effect_class, resource, args, and optional expected_resource_version) and is never executed. The first protected call becomes one unbound proposed_action; unknown tools, extra state/receipt fields and malformed JSON are malformed_result. A response mixing read and protected calls runs none of the reads. Follow-up read results use the Responses previous_response_id/function_call_output protocol.
  • Limits and usage. The adapter checks the request's turns, tool calls, token budget and deadline around each provider call, sends the remaining budget as max_output_tokens, bounds the provider timeout and disables SDK retries. Provider input/output/ total usage and cached input tokens are summed over turns; missing usage is marked estimated, and a provider failure keeps usage from turns that returned with source unknown.
  • Failures. Provider timeouts are adapter_timeout, other provider exceptions are provider_error, malformed Responses output is malformed_result, and a refusal message is refused with model_refused. Provider text, tool names, arguments and exception messages are not copied to results or logs.

OpenAI Agents governed step (B08.openai-agents, #728)#

OpenAIAgentsWorkflowExecutor.run_step runs one bounded governed step through the optional OpenAI Agents SDK; the adapter is caliber.workflows.step_openai_agents and the legacy run_agent path is unchanged. The SDK is loaded lazily through the executor and the ordinary conformance tests use a deterministic offline SDK stub.

  • Tools. Read tools are exposed with their normal function schema and are executed only from step_input.read_tools. Protected tools are exposed with the strict proposal envelope (connector, connector_version, effect_class, resource, args, and optional expected_resource_version). Their callback records the model's claim and returns a fixed acknowledgment; it never resolves or calls the protected binding. The first protected call becomes one unbound proposed_action; malformed JSON, unknown envelope fields (state or receipt_id) and invalid action values are malformed_result.
  • Limits and usage. The request's deadline is checked before the provider call, max_turns is passed to the Agents Runner, max_tool_calls stops read callbacks before another read runs, and provider usage above max_tokens returns max_tokens with the usage retained. Provider input/output/total usage and cached input tokens are summed over raw SDK responses; when the SDK supplies no raw response usage, the adapter marks the bounded estimate as estimated. A read tool the platform refuses because the deadline has passed is not a tool failure: the step ends deadline. The SDK takes max_turns for the run and tool_use_behavior for everything else: the adapter passes a function that, after each turn's tools, ends the run for a recorded proposal, the tool-call limit, a spent token budget (>= max_tokens, as the other adapters) or the deadline, so the model is not asked again after any of them. The SDK is given no handoffs, and a read tool that raises ends the step malformed_result with the exception's text kept out of the result, the log and the model's context. The conformance suite checks all of it, and test_agent_adapter_openai_agents_real_sdk.py runs it on the installed SDK with a scripted model.
  • Failures. Provider timeouts are adapter_timeout, other provider exceptions are provider_error, unreadable SDK output or proposals are malformed_result, a provider refusal is refused with model_refused, and an unavailable optional SDK is refused with provider_unavailable. Provider text, tool arguments and exception messages are not copied to results or logs.

Results recover as for every governed step: a protected proposal proceeds to the approval/binding boundary, provider failures are retried as the next attempt with the reservation kept, and a missing optional SDK is fixed by installing the Agents SDK extra rather than falling back to an ungoverned protected-tool call.

Anthropic governed step (B08.anthropic, #727)#

AnthropicChatWorkflowExecutor.run_step runs one agent step through the Anthropic Messages API; the code is caliber.workflows.step_adapters.anthropic_chat and the executor's run_agent (the ungoverned loop every existing workflow uses) is unchanged. It adds no route, table or setting; the only new option is the executor's step_clock (a test's clock, default UTC now). It takes the step's request and AgentStepInput and answers with the typed result of the section above.

  • Tools. Every tool of the agent is offered to the model, in two kinds. A read tool (a name in step_input.read_tools whose binding does not require approval) is offered with its own input schema, run only from read_tools when called, and its result goes back to the model. Anything else is a proposal: it is offered with the proposal as its input (connector, connector_version, effect_class, resource, the tool's own arguments under args, optional expected_resource_version), is never run, and when the model calls it the step stops with proposed_action carrying that one action. effect_class and connector_version are the model's claims: the action is not platform_bound and bound_to refuses a claim that differs from the platform's. A call of a tool the agent does not have, or a proposal with a field the schema does not define (a state or receipt_id, a model claiming that an effect happened), is malformed_result. When one reply calls several protected tools, the first is proposed and the rest are dropped (v1 allows one action per step); parallel tool use is turned off in the request. A reply that mixes read and protected calls runs none of the reads. Handoff targets are not offered, and a structured-output schema is not applied (a step's result carries no output text).
  • Limits are those of the request, checked around every provider call (the platform checks them again, whatever the adapter reports: central step limits). Before a turn: max_turns, then the deadline, then the tokens left, each a stop reason that keeps the usage so far; before each read tool: max_tool_calls (and the deadline); and no read tool is run when no turn is left to use its result. A call's max_tokens is the smaller of the executor's cap and the tokens left, its timeout the smaller of the provider timeout and the time to the deadline, and the SDK's automatic retries are off (max_retries=0: a retry is the next attempt, which is reserved separately). Provider usage over max_tokens is the max_tokens stop whatever the model said; a reply the provider cut off (stop_reason: "max_tokens") is one too, and a half-finished tool call in it is not acted on. A stop before any call reports zero usage with usage_source: "estimated" (nothing was called).
  • Usage is the provider's, summed over the step's turns, with usage_source: "provider": prompt = input_tokens + cache_creation_input_tokens + cache_read_input_tokens, cached_prompt_tokens = the cache reads (absent when the provider reported none), completion = output_tokens, turns = provider calls, tool_calls = read tools run.
  • Nothing from the provider or the model reaches a result or a log line: no text, tool name, argument or exception message. The log carries the step id, the exception's class name, a fixed reason token and counts.

Results this adapter returns (recover as for any step: the occurrence is retried as the next attempt, after this one's reservation is settled, B08.4):

the provider or modelresultrecover by
calls a protected toolproposed_action with one unbound actionbinding it to the inventory's class (B08.2); nothing was run
calls a read toolthe tool runs from read_tools, the step goes onnothing
times out (TimeoutError, anthropic.APITimeoutError, an httpx/httpcore timeout)error, adapter_timeout, usage of the turns that returned, source unknownretrying as the next attempt; the outcome of the call is unknown and the reservation is kept

The OpenAI chat completions adapter (B08.openai-chat, #729)#

OpenAIChatWorkflowExecutor.run_step runs one governed step through client.chat.completions.create (caliber/src/caliber/workflows/step_openai_chat.py). It uses the message building, reasoning-model handling (including the one retry of the 400 "function tools with reasoning_effort"), prompt-cache keys and tool-call execution helper run_agent uses, and run_agent itself is unchanged. It adds no route, table or setting; the one new constructor argument, step_clock (a callable returning an aware datetime, default the UTC clock), is what a step's deadline is read from.

  • Read tools run only from step_input.read_tools. Any other tool the model calls is never run: it is a proposal. A protected tool is offered to the model with a proposal envelope as its parameters: connector, connector_version, effect_class, resource, args (the tool's own arguments) and optionally expected_resource_version. The envelope is read strictly (an unknown key such as state or receipt_id, a missing or mistyped field or an invalid action is malformed_result), so a model that says an effect happened is unreadable, never recorded. The result is proposed_action with one ProposedAction whose effect_class and connector_version are the model's claims (platform_bound is false; B08.2 binds them to the protected-effect inventory and refuses a mismatch). If one response calls several protected tools the first is proposed and the rest of that response, read calls included, does not run. A call to a tool the agent does not have is malformed_result. The envelope carries the connector the model names: a ProposedAction has no tool-name field, so the platform ties a proposal to the agent's tools through a trusted tool-to-backend map (see the B08.2 section below).
  • Limits come from the request. max_turns counts provider responses; max_tool_calls counts read tools run, all or none per response; max_tokens is compared with the provider's total before each call and after each response (more than the limit stops with max_tokens whatever the model wanted; exactly the limit is allowed but leaves nothing for another call); the deadline is read before each call. A step that may not start (max_* of 0, a deadline reached) returns the stop with zero usage, source estimated, and the provider is not touched. A response the provider cut off (finish_reason: length) is max_tokens and its tool calls are not acted on. Each call is also bounded: the SDK's retries are off (with_options(max_retries=0)), its timeout is the time left to the deadline (at most CALIBER_PROVIDER_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_SECONDS) and the remaining token budget is sent as max_completion_tokens. The platform still enforces the limits against the returned usage (B08.3).
  • Usage is the provider's, summed over turns, with usage_source: "provider" and cached_prompt_tokens only when the provider reported them. A response with no usage object is estimated by word count and reported estimated; a total below prompt + completion is raised to it; a figure that is not a plain non-negative integer (or exceeds 2147483647) is malformed_result. Usage is kept on every stop, and on a failure after at least one response (reported unknown).
  • A refusal is a result. message.refusal and finish_reason: content_filter are refused with model_refused and content_filtered; the model's words are not returned.

No exception text, provider payload, tool name or tool argument is placed in a result or a log line (the log line carries the exception's class name and the step id). Not covered: handoffs (run_agent ignores them too), structured output (a step result has no output field, so the final text is not returned) and the token reservation (B08.4). Recording the proposal is the platform's job and is described in Governed agent steps.

Governed agent steps: a protected action is a proposal (B08.2, #744)#

caliber.effects.step_proposal is what the platform (the interpreter, never an adapter) does with a step that stops with proposed_action. It is switched on per plan: RuntimePlan.governed_agent_steps is a GovernedStepContext. Since #1051 the worker builds one in the reference profile for an admitted run, only for the agent nodes bound to a tool the operator mapped (CALIBER_AGENT_STEP_TOOL_BACKENDS, GovernedStepContext.governed_nodes; see The worker binds the governed path); every other plan, and every other agent node, runs exactly as before. With one, an agent node no longer calls run_agent: it runs through run_agent_step.

  1. The platform classifies the agent's tools; the model's claim decides nothing. registry_tool_classifier answers, for each tool bound to the agent, the protected-effect inventory's class for the tool's registry identity: the binding names its row (resolved_name, resolved_version), the row's module and callable must be the binding's, and is_builtin_tool must accept it (owner, version, module and callable as the seed wrote them). A tool that is not provably CALIBER's own, every MCP tool, an unresolved binding, a missing row and an unreadable registry are the inventory's fail-closed class (irreversible_write). Only tools classified read are handed to the adapter (AgentStepInput.read_tools); every other tool is proposed and never run. A classifier that raises, or answers with anything but a ToolTrust, is the fail-closed class.
  2. The connector comes from a trusted map, never from the proposal. A v1 proposal names no tool, and the connector it names is the model's word, so the platform ties a proposal to the agent through GovernedStepContext.tool_backends: which backend kind (caliber.effects.dispatcher.BACKENDS) each tool sends through, built by the producer from trusted configuration (nothing a model, a manifest author or a tool call writes). It is keyed by the tool's registry identity, (name, version) of the row the binding resolved to (ToolTrust.registry), never by the local name in the manifest: a manifest author can give any tool any local name, so a built-in bound under a mapped name gets no route (the review probe, a regression test). Only the agent's non-read tools whose registry identity is in the map count, and the connector the model named is used for one thing: choosing among them. It must be the connector of a mapped tool's registered backend (connector_not_mapped otherwise; connector_ambiguous if two kinds share it), so a model cannot reach http, or any other registered connector, through a tool that does not send there. The backend kind is then admitted (admit_backend, B12.3a: implementation, capability and configuration pinned in REFERENCE_CONNECTORS; a refusal keeps its own code) and that admission is what submit_proposal requires. Which backends an agent step may reach, and the resource contract. Only backends in step_proposal.AGENT_STEP_BACKENDS (today document_request) are reachable; a tool mapped to any other (http, whose destination is an arbitrary URL and whose egress check runs at dispatch, after an approval would be spent; a registered_tool backend of B04.3, whose configuration resource is the literal template registered-tool/<name>/<version>) is refused, backend_not_for_agent_steps. A reachable backend must declare a resource pattern: its trusted configuration's resource is a regular expression the destination must fully match (resource_not_admitted, also when there is none). The proposal is bound, never trusted. The class is the strictest among the tools that map to that backend (a tool the profile refuses outranks one it dispatches), and the version is the admitted one. ProposedAction.bound_to refuses a claim that differs (claim_mismatch). A mapped tool's destination is still the model's to choose within the connector's pattern. The approval request stores the intent hash and an evidence digest, not the destination: the approver reads the intent from the recorded proposal. Nothing is repaired: a refused proposal records nothing, and the node's retry policy applies.
  3. One effect, one question. submit_proposal records the bound action as a proposed effect for the node's durable occurrence ((run, node, occurrence), the interpreter's occurrence id, so a retry and a restarted run find the same row) and, in the same transaction, create_approval_request records the approval request bound to that exact intent (intent_hash), with an evidence digest over the step, its run and context manifest digests and the intent (step_evidence_hash). The two are written together or not at all. Concurrent proposers of one step serialize on the run row, so exactly one request is live: the second finds the first's instead of superseding it.
  4. The node parks. The step returns blocked (waiting_approval:<node>) with a runtime_approval checkpoint that names the proposal and the request (identifiers and the intent hash, never the action's arguments). The worker parks the run waiting_approval on that very request and creates no node-level duplicate; it refuses to park a run behind a request that is not live and bound to this run, node and proposal. The routes accept the checkpoint kind (runtime_approval), and the parked run is decided by naming the request's runtime_approval_id while the run is waiting_approval at that node (B06.4, #735; the default selection with no id never picks a bound request). The decision does not resume the run: an operator's POST .../resume does, and the dispatcher consumes the approval when the step's effect is claimed (since #1051, by the context's dispatch_approved).
  5. A resumed or retried step does not ask the model again. Before the provider is called the node looks for its occurrence's proposal: committed completes the node, failed fails it, proposed parks it again behind its live request (re-asked when the last one expired, was superseded or was consumed; a rejected request is final, approval_rejected), and any state in between (approved, dispatched, unknown, reconciled: the dispatcher has it) is the existing effect-reconciliation park.

Refusals are EffectRefused with a fixed code and no value from the model; the run error carries only that code.

from caliber.effects.step_proposal import GovernedStepContext, registry_tool_classifier, stored_context_manifest_digest
from caliber.workflows.agent_step import StepCeilings

plan.governed_agent_steps = GovernedStepContext(
    session_factory=session_factory,
    workflow_run_id=run_id,
    run_manifest_digest=run_manifest_digest,           # the stored run manifest's SHA-256
    grant_id=run_manifest["grant_id"],                 # the one grant the step runs under
    classify_tool=registry_tool_classifier(session_factory),
    context_manifest_digest=stored_context_manifest_digest(session_factory, run_id),
    limits=lambda agent: step_limits,                  # the producer's; capped at the ceilings, enforced by the platform (B08.3)
    requested_by=run_initiator,
    approval_ttl_seconds=configured_ttl_seconds(config),
    tool_backends={("request_missing_document", "1.0"): "document_request"},  # registry identity -> backend, the producer's

)

Dispatching an approved proposal is the context's dispatch_approved (#1051): a context without one leaves an approved proposal proposed and the run waiting_approval, as before; the worker's sends it once, under the lease, through the document_request backend. Not covered, so not claimed: model-selected calls of an agent that is not governed (B04.6, #768), handoffs, inline targets and parallel branches (refused), and the output text of a governed step (a step that completes is refused). The v1 proposal still carries no tool name, so within a connector the class is the strictest of the tools that map to it; an additive contract change (the tool name in the envelope) would make it exact. Telling the model the connector, version and class to claim is an adapter concern.

Central step limits: turns, tool calls, tokens and the deadline (B08.3, #752)#

The limits of an agent step (max_turns, max_tool_calls, max_tokens and the deadline of the request) are enforced by the platform in caliber.workflows.agent_step.run_agent_step, the one boundary every adapter goes through, and not by each adapter. The adapters keep their own in-loop checks (they are the only code that can stop a provider call that is under way), but the platform does not rely on them and does not take an adapter's or a model's word for what a step used. It adds no table, route or migration.

Where the limits come from. GovernedStepContext.limits(agent) is the producer's (trusted run or step configuration, never anything the adapter, the manifest author or the model supplies). The interpreter then brings them down to the platform's ceilings (GovernedStepContext.ceilings, default StepCeilings(), built from settings with StepCeilings.from_config(config)) with cap_limits: a count above its ceiling becomes the ceiling, a deadline later than now + CALIBER_AGENT_STEP_MAX_SECONDS is brought forward to it (an earlier deadline is kept exactly as given), and a limit is never raised. A producer whose limits raises, returns anything but a StepLimits, or names a deadline that is not an RFC 3339 instant stops the step with governed agent step limits unavailable: limits_invalid before the adapter is touched (no text from the producer's failure); a context clock that is not an aware instant stops it with governed agent step clock unavailable: clock_invalid. The request schema's own bound is 2147483647; the ceilings are what make a step finite in practice.

SettingDefaultAcceptedMeaning
CALIBER_AGENT_STEP_MAX_TURNS251 to 1000The most provider turns one step may be given.
CALIBER_AGENT_STEP_MAX_TOOL_CALLS500 to 1000The most read-tool calls one step may make (0 allows none).
CALIBER_AGENT_STEP_MAX_TOKENS2000001 to 10000000The most tokens (prompt plus completion) one step may use.
CALIBER_AGENT_STEP_MAX_SECONDS6001 to 86400, finiteThe longest window, from the moment the step is asked, a deadline may reach.

A value outside its bounds stops the service at startup, naming the setting. Like the context caps, the ceilings reach a live step once the producer of the governed context passes StepCeilings.from_config(config); a context that names none is capped at these defaults, never uncapped.

What the boundary does, for every adapter alike:

  1. Before work (before_work_stop): a step with max_turns of 0, with max_tokens of 0, or whose deadline is now or past (on the platform's clock) stops with that reason and the adapter is not called: zero usage, usage_source: "estimated" (nothing was called; the interpreter checks this before it reserves, so a step stopped here reserves nothing, B08.4). max_tool_calls of 0 does not stop a step: it may still answer without a tool.
  2. During work: every read tool the adapter is handed (its own and its handoff targets') goes through a platform counter. The call past max_tool_calls is refused with StepToolBudgetExceeded (the tool does not run, the text is fixed), and two calls racing for the last slot cannot both run. A read tool called at or after the deadline (on the platform's monotonic-based clock) is refused the same way with StepDeadlineReached (the tool does not run, the call is not counted), and the step ends deadline even if the adapter ignores the refusal; a tool call already running is not interrupted. An adapter receives its own copy of the request, so rewriting the limits of the request it holds changes nothing the platform checks.
  3. After work: a completed or proposed_action result is replaced by the stop of the limit it passed, its proposal dropped (a step that overran never gets to propose, so no proposal row and no approval request exist), when its reported turns, tool_calls or total_tokens is over the limit, when the platform counted a tool call past the limit (even if the adapter swallowed the refusal and reported fewer), or when the platform's own clock says the step finished after its deadline. Several limits passed are named in the order max_turns, max_tool_calls, max_tokens, deadline. The usage kept is the reported one (what was spent is recorded), with tool_calls raised to the platform's own count when that is higher. A refused, error or limit stop the adapter reports itself is returned as it is.

Exactly the limit is within it. max_tokens: 100 with total_tokens: 100 completes; 101 stops with max_tokens. The same holds for turns and tool calls. A deadline stops a step that is at or past it before work, and one that finished after it after work (finishing exactly at the deadline is within it). The deadline is read from StepClock: the absolute deadline against wall time at the start, and how long the step took against a monotonic clock, so a wall clock stepped mid-step (an NTP correction) can neither extend nor spuriously cut a step. Tests inject a fake clock; a clock that is not an aware instant, or whose monotonic reading is not a finite number, is refused with ValueError before the adapter runs.
